inspection_summary: Inspected all 619 normalized lines of Bombieri's survey. The source develops the classical zeta/RH statement, the prime-distribution transform route, the enlargement to global L-functions, three distinct kinds of evidence, the finite-field analogy already captured by v1, Weil's explicit-formula trace dictionary already captured by v1, and subsequent index-theoretic, spectral, and missing-geometry questions. Formula glyph loss is localized and explicitly flagged; the exact test-function criterion at lines 468-479 is not reconstructed.

sections_inspected.label: I. The problem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the analytic zeta package, xi reformulation, trivial/nontrivial zeros, and the Riemann hypothesis.

sections_inspected.label: II. History and significance
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Traces the Euler-product, Chebyshev, and Riemann transform mechanisms, identifies the prime-counting error meaning of RH, and broadens the problem to global L-functions.

sections_inspected.label: III. Evidence for the Riemann hypothesis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates finite-range numerical certification, zero-density bounds, and positive-proportion critical-line results.

sections_inspected.label: IV. Varieties over finite fields
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the curve-zeta and Frobenius-cohomology analogy; this exact span is represented by the carried v1 finite-field unit.

sections_inspected.label: V. Explicit formula and prospective mechanisms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Gives the carried v1 explicit trace dictionary, then develops an OCR-sensitive negativity criterion, the readable algebraic index mechanism, spectral statistics, and missing global analogues.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic apparatus only; inspected for boundary completeness and not selected as semantic units.

accepted_units.title: The analytic zeta package and the critical-line statement
accepted_units.why_material: Places RH inside analytic continuation, the functional equation, the xi transformation, and the separation of trivial from nontrivial zeros, so the conjecture is a structural location statement rather than an isolated slogan.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose supports the transformation and zero-location roles. Exact displays should be checked against the scan before formula-level reuse.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-bearing: extraction loses the real-part glyph and visually collapses 1/2 in several places; do not normalize those formulas from memory.

accepted_units.title: Euler product turns zeta into a prime-distribution object
accepted_units.why_material: The product factorization is the basic semantic bridge from an analytic function to prime-local factors and motivates later logarithmic and explicit-formula transforms.
accepted_units.context_note: Historical attribution is supporting context; the reusable content is the product-to-primes representation change.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The product is legible, but the real-part condition contains a damaged glyph; scan verification is required for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Boundary smoothness forces the coefficients of any finite prime-counting asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: Tchebychev's route links the logarithm of the Euler product and regularity at the pole to a rigidity statement: if a finite logarithmic asymptotic exists, its coefficients must match those of Li.
accepted_units.context_note: The conceptual implication is explicit in prose even though displayed equations (2) and (3) have extraction damage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: summation layout, powers, and integral typography are damaged; use the prose-supported regularity-to-coefficient mechanism only pending scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Weighted prime counts connect analytic counting to exact combinatorial identities
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction of theta and psi and an exact factorial identity shows how a weighted representation can yield rigorous upper and lower bounds of the correct order without assuming the full asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinction between weighted counting and direct pi counting is reusable; the exact identity needs its original typesetting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: radicals, indices, and the factorial identity are visibly scrambled, so no exact formula is reconstructed.

accepted_units.title: Riemann's transform-residue pipeline makes zeros control primes
accepted_units.why_material: The source gives a reusable sequence of representation changes: integral continuation, logarithmic Euler product, integral transform, Fourier inversion, residue evaluation, and inversion back to prime counting.
accepted_units.context_note: Selected for the conceptual pipeline rather than the exact displayed transforms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several integral and weighted-count displays lose symbols or layout; the prose specifies the pipeline, while exact formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: RH fixes the scale of prime-counting deviation from its mean
accepted_units.why_material: This passage explains why the zero-location conjecture is central: it is equivalent to a sharply controlled error around Li, near the scale forced by known oscillation, while failure would disrupt prime distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: The source's historical quotation is retained because it contrasts immediate proof need with the later-recognized error-term significance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The square-root and 1/2 typography is degraded; retain the semantic equivalence and request scan verification for the exact bound.

accepted_units.title: Zeta is a prototype whose zeros encode global arithmetic objects
accepted_units.why_material: The survey reframes RH as one instance of a global L-function package with Euler products, functional equations, local Ramanujan properties, and arithmetic information encoded at zeros, poles, and special values.
accepted_units.context_note: The listed consequences illustrate scope rather than providing proofs of those consequences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant and recoverable from the normalized text; no exact formula dependency.

accepted_units.title: For elliptic-curve L-functions, modularity supplies the analytic package that direct analysis cannot
accepted_units.why_material: The passage isolates a major bottleneck: functional equations may be equivalent to geometric/modular parametrization, shifting the hard work from analytic manipulation to proving modularity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a structural comparison, not a claim that modularity automatically resolves RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; the subgroup notation is extraction-sensitive but not essential to the selected mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Maass L-functions block a purely arithmetic-geometric framing
accepted_units.why_material: Primitive Maass waveforms produce Euler-product L-functions expected to satisfy RH-like statements despite lacking a direct arithmetic or geometric origin, motivating a genuinely general solution route.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion is explicitly provisional: greater generality and new ideas may be necessary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed Dirichlet-series summation mark is lost near lines 249-250; use only the prose-supported eigenvalue-series role pending scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Independent zero counting plus critical-line sign changes certifies a finite RH window
accepted_units.why_material: The protocol separates a total zero count obtained from the argument principle from detected odd-order critical-line zeros; equality certifies completeness in the rectangle rather than merely sampling apparent zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The reported historical computation is evidence in a bounded range, not a proof of the unrestricted conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: the Cauchy-integral display is damaged, but the surrounding prose states the integer count, numerical evaluation, sign-change census, and equality check; verify the display against the scan before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Target difficult heights and broaden L-function families without mistaking finite evidence for proof
accepted_units.why_material: The passage combines an extrema reformulation, a heuristic for where counterexamples might hide, high-altitude spot checks, spacing evidence, and tests in other L-function families while preserving their finite empirical status.
accepted_units.context_note: This is useful as adversarial test-selection logic, not as unrestricted validation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The critical-line zeta expression is split across lines 299-301 and powers are visually collapsed; exact numerical/formula claims require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero-density bounds quantify how rare off-line exceptions must be
accepted_units.why_material: Counting zeros to the right of a movable boundary yields progressively sublinear density estimates with arithmetic consequences, furnishing graded evidence short of pointwise RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The semantic distinction between density control and exclusion of every exception is essential.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-sensitive: 1/2 and 3/4 are collapsed and exponents are layout-dependent; no exact bound should be copied without scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A positive proportion of simple critical-line zeros transfers across major L-function classes
accepted_units.why_material: This is a qualitatively different partial result from density bounds: it proves many zeros lie simply on the target line and notes extension to Dirichlet, modular, and Maass settings.
accepted_units.context_note: The source reports the then-known proportion and extensions; it does not imply that all zeros lie on the line.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; the percentage is readable, with bibliographic verification available only outside this bounded task.

accepted_units.title: The algebraic index theorem supplies the geometric negativity mechanism
accepted_units.why_material: For curves over finite fields, the source identifies the negativity needed by the preceding explicit-formula criterion as a consequence of a negative-semidefinite divisor intersection form, and explains the algebraic and Hodge-theoretic proof landscape.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact test-function criterion at lines 468-479 is extraction-defective and is not reconstructed; this unit starts from the source's readable assertion of the geometric consequence and includes the stated index theorem and its limits.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The intersection-form theorem is readable in prose. Its linkage to the exact analytic criterion remains scan-dependent because the preceding formulas are damaged.

accepted_units.title: Universal spacing statistics motivate a self-adjoint spectral model
accepted_units.why_material: Observed and conjectured zero-spacing universality aligns L-function families with random-matrix spectra and the Hilbert-Polya operator viewpoint, while finite-field family results provide an unconditional analogue.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage supplies compatibility and analogy, not construction of the operator or proof of RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant and readable; named results are used only as source-reported evidence.

accepted_units.title: The classical case lacks global analogues of cohomology, Frobenius, and the index theorem
accepted_units.why_material: The survey distills the analogy into concrete missing structures and then stress-tests it with Maass L-functions, for which no guiding geometric model is available.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed adelic directions are explicitly characterized as conjectural glimpses, not established machinery.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant and recoverable; the overlap with the Severi footnote preserves the local transition from index mechanism to open global questions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From Euler factors to prime-counting fluctuations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Successive representation changes turn prime-local factorization into transform data whose singularities and zeros govern both the mean and fluctuation scale of prime counts.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This source outlines the mechanisms and damaged displays rather than supplying a self-contained derivation of every formula.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Three non-interchangeable evidence channels
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Finite-window certification, density control of possible exceptions, and positive-proportion critical-line theorems constrain RH in logically different ways and should not be collapsed into a single confidence score.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: None excludes every off-line zero; finite computations and partial theorems remain bounded evidence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why the solution may need a general theory without being purely geometric
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The common L-function package pushes toward a general structural theory, but the modularity bottleneck and non-geometric Maass examples show that importing finite-field geometry alone cannot be assumed sufficient.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source poses this as motivation and obstruction, not as a settled architecture for a proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Geometric negativity and spectrality as complementary clues
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The finite-field index theorem supplies a positivity/negativity mechanism while spacing universality suggests self-adjoint spectrality; the classical problem is precisely that the corresponding global objects and theorem remain unidentified.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The analytic criterion immediately preceding the index discussion is extraction-defective, and neither clue constructs the missing classical structure.
